• **Chapter Introduction:** Welcome to Chapter 5 of the DAV Class LKG EVS curriculum, focusing on "Plants, Green Leaves & Flowers," designed to introduce young learners to the vibrant world of botany and nature.
• **Scope of Study:** This comprehensive study note explores the fundamental characteristics of plants, the vital role of green leaves, and the beauty and diversity of flowers found in our immediate environment.
• **Target Audience Focus:** Tailored for LKG students of the Dayanand Anglo-Vedic Public School Board, utilizing simple, age-appropriate scientific concepts to build foundational observational skills.
• **Definition of a Plant:** **Plant**: A living organism that grows in the ground, possesses roots, stems, and leaves, and typically makes its own food using sunlight.
• **Living Nature:** Plants are living things just like humans and animals, meaning they breathe, grow, need food and water, and respond to their environment.
• **Ubiquity of Plants:** Plants are found everywhere around us—in gardens, parks, schoolyards, forests, and even inside our homes as potted decorations.
• **Basic Plant Parts:** A typical plant consists of underground roots, an upright stem, spreading branches, green leaves, and colorful flowers.
• **The Soil Connection:** Most plants grow firmly in the soil, which acts as their anchor and primary source of water and essential mineral nutrients.
• **Natural Environment:** Plants form an integral part of our natural ecosystem, providing beauty, fresh air, shade, and habitats for various small creatures.
• **Observation Skills:** Young learners are encouraged to observe plants daily, noticing differences in size, shape, color, and texture of various plant parts.
• **Gentle Interaction:** DAV values teach respect for nature; children learn that plants are our green friends and should be cared for gently without plucking them needlessly.
• **Sunlight Dependency:** Plants require natural sunlight to survive, grow healthily, and perform their daily biological processes.
• **Water Requirements:** Water is essential for plants; it travels from the roots up through the stem to keep the entire plant hydrated and upright.
• **Fresh Air Production:** Plants play a crucial role in cleaning the air around us, releasing fresh oxygen that humans and animals need to breathe.
• **Green Cover:** The presence of plants creates a green cover on the earth, making our surroundings look beautiful, peaceful, and pleasant.

-

• **Classification of Plants:** Plants come in various sizes, shapes, and types, ranging from tiny grass blades to massive, towering trees in forests.
• **Big Plants (Trees):** **Tree**: A large, tall plant with a very thick, hard, woody brown stem called a trunk and numerous strong branches.
• **Examples of Trees:** Common trees include the Banyan tree, Neem tree, Mango tree, and Peepal tree, which provide extensive shade and shelter.
• **The Trunk Concept:** The trunk of a tree acts as its strong pillar, supporting the heavy weight of branches, leaves, fruits, and flowers high up in the air.
• **Medium Plants (Shrubs):** **Shrub**: A medium-sized, bushy plant with multiple hard, woody stems growing close to the ground, smaller than a tree.
• **Examples of Shrubs:** Familiar shrubs include the Rose plant, Hibiscus, Jasmine, and Cotton plant, known for their dense and bushy appearance.
• **Small Plants (Herbs):** **Herb**: A very small plant with a soft, green, and tender stem, usually living for a short season.
• **Examples of Herbs:** Grass, Mint (Pudina), Coriander (Dhania), and Spinach are classic examples of delicate herbaceous plants.
• **Climber Plants:** **Climber**: A plant with a very weak, thin, and soft stem that cannot stand straight on its own and needs support to grow upwards.
• **Support Mechanisms:** Climbers use walls, sticks, fences, or other trees to climb and reach towards sunlight, utilizing specialized structures like tendrils.
• **Examples of Climbers:** Money plant, Pea plant, Grapevine, and Bean plant are popular climbers easily observed in home gardens.
• **Creeper Plants:** **Creeper**: A plant with a weak stem that spreads horizontally along the ground instead of standing upright or climbing upwards.
• **Examples of Creepers:** Watermelon, Pumpkin, Musk melon, and Strawberry plants are typical creepers that bear heavy fruits on the soil surface.
• **Water Plants (Aquatic Plants):** **Aquatic Plant**: Special types of plants that grow, live, and reproduce completely inside or on the surface of water bodies like ponds and lakes.
• **Examples of Water Plants:** Lotus and Water Lily are beautiful aquatic plants with broad leaves floating gracefully on water surfaces.

-

• **Introduction to Green Leaves:** **Leaf**: A flat, thin, green structure attached to the stem or branches of a plant, serving as the primary food factory.
• **Predominant Color:** The most striking feature of healthy leaves is their vibrant green color, which comes from a special pigment found inside them.
• **Chlorophyll Concept:** **Chlorophyll**: The natural green substance present inside plant leaves that captures sunlight and gives leaves their characteristic color.
• **Variety of Shapes:** Leaves are not all identical; they come in a fascinating variety of shapes including oval, round, needle-like, heart-shaped, and lance-like.
• **Variety of Sizes:** Leaf sizes range from microscopic scales to enormous palm fronds, depending entirely on the species of the plant.
• **Leaf Margins:** The edges of leaves (margins) can be completely smooth, wavy, jagged, or toothed like a saw, offering clues for plant identification.
• **Leaf Texture:** The surface texture of leaves varies greatly; some are smooth and glossy, while others feel rough, fuzzy, velvety, or leathery.
• **Leaf Venation (Lines):** If observed closely, leaves feature a network of fine lines running across their surface, which transport water and nutrients.
• **The Main Vein (Midrib):** **Midrib**: The prominent central line running right down the middle of a leaf, providing structural strength and support.
• **Food Makers (Photosynthesis Intro):** Leaves are often called the "kitchen of the plant" because they use sunlight, air, and water to prepare food for the entire organism.
• **Breathing Organs:** Leaves have tiny, microscopic openings on their underside that allow the plant to take in air and release fresh oxygen into the atmosphere.
• **Fallen Leaves:** As leaves age, they turn yellow, orange, or brown, detach from the stem, fall to the ground, and eventually enrich the soil naturally.
• **Uses of Leaves for Humans:** Humans use various leaves for multiple purposes, including cooking flavor (curry leaves, bay leaves), serving food (banana leaves), and medicine (tulsi).
• **Animal Diargies (Herbivores):** Many animals, such as cows, goats, elephants, and caterpillars, depend entirely on eating fresh green leaves for their nutrition.
• **Observational Activity:** LKG students are encouraged to collect fallen green leaves of different shapes and sizes to paste in their nature scrapbooks.

-

• **The Wonders of Flowers:** **Flower**: The most attractive, colorful, and fragrant part of a plant, often referred to as its reproductive structure and bloom.
• **Visual Appeal:** Flowers are celebrated for their dazzling array of colors, including bright reds, sunny yellows, pure whites, deep purples, and soft pinks.
• **Pleasing Fragrances:** Many flowers produce sweet, pleasant scents (fragrance) that attract insects, bees, butterflies, and humans alike.
• **Structural Variety:** Flowers differ vastly in structure; some have single rows of wide petals, while others have multiple layers forming complex, beautiful rosettes.
• **The Rose:** **Rose**: A popular woody shrub flower known for its velvety petals, sweet fragrance, and protective thorns on its stem, available in red, pink, yellow, and white.
• **The Lotus:** **Lotus**: The national flower of India, growing gracefully in muddy water ponds with broad pink or white petals symbolizing purity and beauty.
• **The Sunflower:** **Sunflower**: A large, bright yellow flower that gets its name because its wide face constantly turns to follow the movement of the sun across the sky.
• **The Marigold:** **Marigold (Gainda):** A common Indian festival flower featuring clusters of bright orange or yellow ruffled petals used extensively in decorations and garlands.
• **The Jasmine:** **Jasmine (Mogra):** A small, delicate, star-shaped white flower renowned for its intensely sweet nighttime fragrance, often woven into hair adornments.
• **The Hibiscus:** **Hibiscus (Japa):** A large, trumpet-shaped tropical flower with prominent stamens, commonly found in bright red shades in temple courtyards.
• **Petal Definition:** **Petal**: The thin, colorful, and often soft outer segments of a flower designed specifically to attract pollinating insects and birds.
• **Bud to Bloom Process:** **Bud**: The tight, unopened, green-enclosed immature stage of a flower that gradually uncurls and blossoms into a full flower.
• **Nectar Production:** Flowers produce a sweet sugary liquid called nectar deep inside their petals, which serves as food for bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds.
• **Pollination Helpers:** Insects visiting flowers to drink nectar inadvertently carry pollen grains from one flower to another, helping plants produce seeds and fruits.
• **Transition to Fruit:** Once a flower's job is complete, its colorful petals wither and fall off, and the remaining base swells up to transform into a delicious fruit.

-

• **Comprehensive Plant Parts Review:** Every part of a plant—roots, stem, leaves, flowers, and fruits—has a specific, vital job to keep the plant alive and healthy.
• **Root System Deep Dive:** **Roots**: The underground part of the plant that grows downward into the soil, drinking up water and vital minerals like a straw.
• **Stem System Deep Dive:** **Stem**: The upright, pillar-like main body of the plant above the ground that supports branches, leaves, and flowers, acting as a transport highway.
• **Leaf System Recap:** **Leaf**: The flat green food factory that uses sunlight to cook meals for the plant, ensuring continuous growth and development.
• **Flower System Recap:** **Flower**: The blooming, colorful beauty of the plant that attracts helpful insects and eventually creates seeds for new baby plants.
• **Seed to Plant Cycle:** **Seed**: A tiny, hard capsule containing a baby plant inside, which sprouts when planted in soil, given water, and warmed by sunlight.
• **Germination Concept:** **Germination**: The magical process by which a tiny seed cracks open underground, sends down roots, and pushes a green shoot up into the air.
• **Four Basic Needs:** For any plant to grow from a seed into a mature, leaf-and-flower-bearing adult, it strictly requires four key things: soil, water, air, and sunlight.
• **The Role of Sunlight:** Sunlight provides the vital energy that green leaves need to mix water and air together to cook food, acting like solar power.
• **The Role of Air:** Plants take in carbon dioxide gas from the air through their leaves and release fresh oxygen back into the atmosphere for us.
• **The Role of Water:** Water hydrates plant cells, carries dissolved soil nutrients up the stem, and keeps soft leaves and stems crisp and upright.
• **The Role of Soil:** Soil anchors the plant firmly in place so it doesn't blow away in the wind, while storing moisture and nutrients for the roots.
• **Seasonal Changes:** Many plants change according to seasons; trees shed leaves in autumn, bloom profusely in spring, and bear fruit in summer.
• **Evergreen vs. Deciduous:** Some plants stay green and leafy all year round (evergreen), while others lose all their leaves during dry or cold winter months.
• **Nature's Balance:** Plants maintain the ecological balance of the planet, ensuring that air remains breathable, soil remains stable, and herbivores have food.

-

• **Human Dependence on Plants:** Human beings rely entirely on plants for survival, deriving food, clothing fibers, shelter timber, medicines, and oxygen from them.
• **Plant Foods (Vegetables):** We eat various parts of plants as vegetables, including roots (carrots, radishes), stems (potatoes, celery), and leaves (spinach, cabbage).
• **Plant Foods (Fruits):** Delicious, juicy fruits such as apples, bananas, mangoes, and oranges are gifts from flowering plants, packed with vitamins and energy.
• **Cereals and Grains:** Major food grains like wheat, rice, corn, and pulses (dal) that form our daily meals come from cultivated farm crops and cereal plants.
• **Medicinal Plants:** **Medicinal Plant**: Special plants utilized in traditional healthcare and modern medicine to cure illnesses, heal wounds, and promote wellness.
• **Tulsi (Holy Basil):** A sacred medicinal plant found in Indian courtyards whose leaves are used to cure colds, coughs, and boost human immunity.
• **Aloe Vera:** A thick, succulent plant whose gel-like leaf interior is used to heal skin burns, moisturize skin, and soothe minor cuts.
• **Neem Tree Value:** Every part of the Neem tree—bark, leaves, seeds, and roots—possesses powerful germ-fighting, antiseptic, and medicinal properties.
• **Wood and Timber:** Large trees provide strong wood (timber) used by humans to build houses, manufacture furniture, craft doors, and construct boats.
• **Paper Production:** Wood pulp extracted from fast-growing trees is processed in factories to manufacture paper, notebooks, textbooks, and newspapers we use daily.
• **Clothing Fibers:** Plants like cotton provide soft, breathable natural fibers spun into threads and woven into comfortable summer clothes and bedsheets.
• **Jute Bags and Ropes:** The rough fibrous stems of the jute plant are twisted into durable ropes, gunny sacks, eco-friendly shopping bags, and doormats.
• **Perfumes and Oils:** Fragrant flowers like jasmine, rose, and lavender are distilled to extract essential oils used in perfumes, soaps, and cosmetics.
• **Beverages:** Popular daily drinks like tea and coffee are manufactured by processing the leaves of tea bushes and roasted seeds of coffee plants.
• **Rubber and Gums:** Sticky sap tapped from rubber trees is processed to make erasers, tires, and balloons, while natural tree gums are used in adhesives.

-

• **Animal Dependence on Plants:** Animals, birds, insects, and reptiles depend heavily on plants for their daily survival, shelter, and breeding grounds.
• **Herbivorous Animals:** **Herbivore**: An animal that feeds exclusively on plant materials such as grass, leaves, tender twigs, bark, flowers, and fruits.
• **Examples of Herbivores:** Majestic elephants, gentle giraffes, cows, deer, horses, and rabbits survive entirely on plant-based diets for their energy.
• **Bird Habitats:** Trees serve as natural high-rise apartment complexes for birds, offering safe, sturdy branches to build nests, lay eggs, and raise chicks.
• **Insects and Flowers:** Bees, butterflies, and beetles visit colorful flowers constantly to feed on sweet nectar and pollen, establishing a vital symbiotic relationship.
• **Monkey Shelters:** Monkeys, squirrels, and tree-dwelling rodents live entirely in the canopy of large trees, finding safety from ground predators and abundant food.
• **Camouflage and Protection:** Small insects, caterpillars, and green grasshoppers blend seamlessly into green leaves and bushes to hide from hungry predators.
• **Aquatic Animal Shelters:** Underwater plants provide oxygen, shade, and hiding spots for fish, tadpoles, and other aquatic creatures living in ponds and rivers.
• **Seed Dispersal by Animals:** Animals eat juicy fruits, swallow seeds, and drop them far away in their droppings, helping new plants grow in distant locations.
• **Food Chain Foundation:** Plants occupy the very first foundational level of every natural food chain, feeding herbivores, which in turn feed carnivores.
• **Ecosystem Stability:** Without plants, animal populations would rapidly collapse due to starvation, lack of oxygen, and complete loss of natural shelters.
• **Forest Ecosystems:** Dense forests teeming with thousands of plant species support millions of unique animal and insect species in a balanced web of life.
• **Grazing Fields:** Open grassy meadows provide grazing grounds for wild herds, illustrating the essential role of simple herbaceous ground cover.
• **Nectar Dependence:** Without flowering plants, pollinating insect species like honeybees would face extinction, directly threatening global food production.
• **Observational Learning:** Children are encouraged during nature walks to spot birds sitting on trees or butterflies resting on flowers to witness animal-plant bonds.

-

• **Caring for Plants:** Just as humans need love, food, and water, young plants require attentive care, protection, and nurturing to grow into healthy adults.
• **Watering Routine:** **Watering**: The act of pouring water gently over the soil around a plant's roots, ensuring it stays hydrated without getting waterlogged.
• **Using Proper Tools:** LKG children learn to use small, child-safe watering cans to sprinkle water evenly over potted plants in their school garden.
• **Sunlight Placement:** Potted indoor plants must be placed near sunny windowsills or balconies where they can receive adequate daily sunlight for their leaves.
• **Weeding the Soil:** **Weeding**: The process of removing unwanted, wild plants (weeds) that steal valuable water and soil nutrients from our cultivated plants.
• **Gentle Handling Rule:** DAV values emphasize plant conservation; students are taught never to snap branches, tear green leaves, or pluck flowers needlessly.
• **Protecting Young Saplings:** **Sapling**: A young, fragile baby tree that needs wooden stakes and protective fences to shield it from stray animals and harsh winds.
• **Planting Trees (Afforestation):** **Afforestation**: The act of planting new saplings in large numbers to increase forest cover, improve air quality, and green our neighborhoods.
• **Celebration Days:** Schools celebrate special eco-friendly events like Van Mahotsav, where students plant saplings and take personal oaths to protect nature.
• **Composting Organic Waste:** Fallen dry leaves, vegetable peels, and fruit waste can be recycled into rich organic compost to nourish garden soil naturally.
• **Avoiding Plastic Litter:** Throwing plastic bags and wrappers around plant roots suffocates the soil; children learn to keep plant beds clean and litter-free.
• **Protecting from Pests:** Observing plants for tiny crawling pests or damaged leaves and reporting them to gardeners or teachers keeps plants healthy.
• **The Joy of Growing:** Watching a tiny seed sprout, grow green leaves, and finally bloom into a colorful flower brings immense joy and satisfaction to children.
• **Responsibility Building:** Caring for a classroom potted plant teaches young LKG learners patience, empathy, duty, and responsibility toward living creatures.
• **Green School Initiative:** The DAV Public School Board promotes green campuses where every student actively participates in maintaining clean, lush herbal gardens.

-

• **Key Vocabulary Review (Plant):** **Plant**: A living green thing with roots, stems, leaves, and flowers that grows in soil and makes its own food.
• **Key Vocabulary Review (Tree):** **Tree**: A tall, massive plant with a thick, hard, woody brown trunk and many spreading branches providing shade.
• **Key Vocabulary Review (Shrub):** **Shrub**: A medium-sized, bushy plant featuring multiple hard woody stems growing close to the ground, like a rose bush.
• **Key Vocabulary Review (Herb):** **Herb**: A very small, delicate plant with a soft, green, tender stem, such as grass, mint, or coriander.
• **Key Vocabulary Review (Climber):** **Climber**: A weak-stemmed plant that requires external support like walls or sticks to grow upwards toward sunlight.
• **Key Vocabulary Review (Creeper):** **Creeper**: A weak plant with trailing stems that spreads horizontally across the surface of the ground, bearing heavy fruits.
• **Key Vocabulary Review (Root):** **Root**: The underground anchor of a plant that drinks water and mineral nutrients from the surrounding soil.
• **Key Vocabulary Review (Stem):** **Stem**: The upright, supporting axis of a plant above ground that transports water and food to all parts.
• **Key Vocabulary Review (Leaf):** **Leaf**: The flat, green food-making factory of the plant containing chlorophyll and tiny breathing pores.
• **Key Vocabulary Review (Chlorophyll):** **Chlorophyll**: The natural green coloring pigment inside leaves that traps sunlight to help the plant cook food.
• **Key Vocabulary Review (Flower):** **Flower**: The colorful, attractive, and fragrant bloom of a plant that develops into seeds and fruits.
• **Key Vocabulary Review (Bud):** **Bud**: The tight, unopened, immature stage of a flower protected by tiny green outer leaves before blooming.
• **Key Vocabulary Review (Petal):** **Petal**: The soft, brightly colored outer segment of a flower designed to attract visiting pollinating insects.
• **Key Vocabulary Review (Seed):** **Seed**: A hard, tiny capsule containing a baby plant waiting for soil, water, and sunlight to germinate.
• **Key Vocabulary Review (Sapling):** **Sapling**: A young, tender baby tree requiring special care, watering, and protection to grow strong.

-

• **Chapter Summary:** Chapter 5 ("Plants, Green Leaves & Flowers") successfully instills foundational botanical knowledge and ecological awareness in Class LKG students.
• **Core Takeaway 1:** Students learn that plants are living organisms encompassing diverse forms, including giant trees, bushy shrubs, tiny herbs, climbers, and creepers.
• **Core Takeaway 2:** The chapter emphasizes the vital role of green leaves as the food-producing factories of plants, driven by sunlight and chlorophyll.
• **Core Takeaway 3:** Young learners explore the spectacular beauty, colors, and fragrances of flowers such as roses, lotuses, sunflowers, marigolds, and jasmines.
• **Core Takeaway 4:** The essential requirements for plant survival—soil, water, air, and sunlight—are highlighted through simple, relatable, child-friendly explanations.
• **Core Takeaway 5:** The profound interdependence between plants, humans, and animals is demonstrated, showing how plants provide food, oxygen, timber, and shelter.
• **Core Takeaway 6:** DAV value education principles are seamlessly integrated, teaching children respect, empathy, gentleness, and active responsibility toward nature.
• **Observational Mastery:** LKG students develop keen visual observation skills by identifying different leaf shapes, flower colors, and plant sizes in their school environment.
• **Interactive Learning:** Hands-on activities like nature walks, leaf collection, seed observation, and watering classroom plants reinforce theoretical concepts effectively.
• **Foundational Science:** This chapter lays a rock-solid foundation for future environmental studies and advanced biological sciences in higher primary classes.
• **Curricular Alignment:** Fully aligned with the Dayanand Anglo-Vedic Public School Board academic framework, fostering holistic growth and eco-consciousness from early childhood.
• **Teacher Guidance Note:** Educators are encouraged to use flashcards, real plant specimens, school garden visits, and storytelling to keep learning engaging and interactive.
• **Parental Involvement:** Parents can reinforce learning at home by encouraging children to water balcony plants, observe blooming flowers, and maintain a nature scrapbook.
• **Lifelong Appreciation:** By understanding plants, green leaves, and flowers early in life, children develop a lifelong love and reverence for the natural world.
• **Conclusion:** Mastery of Chapter 5 empowers LKG students to step forward as young, knowledgeable guardians of the environment and proud ambassadors of DAV green initiatives.
